title: Helmet Headset
tagline: A cheap Bluetooth neckband taken apart and rebuilt as a helmet headset
summary: Music, calls and navigation voice in your helmet for about ₹2,000–4,000 instead of a ₹5,000+ communicator. A cheap Bluetooth neckband already has the hard parts (Bluetooth, the amplifier, the mic circuit, charging, the battery): this project moves them to better places. Its board, battery and buttons go in a slim pod stuck to the outside of the shell on the left with VHB tape (3 big rubber buttons for gloves, sealed, USB-C at the back); 40 mm speakers in printed pucks go in the liner's ear pockets; the mic goes on a bendable boom held on the helmet's fixed part, so a modular helmet's chin bar flips up over it. No holes in the helmet. General purpose: the helmet's curve, the neckband's parts and the speakers are settings.
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). Designed first for a modular (flip-up) helmet. The neckband (boAt Rockerz 255 Pro+) has no published teardown: open yours and measure its board and battery first.
see_sub: The pod on the left, behind the chin bar's pivot (the helmet is a plain stand-in); inside, the speakers in the ear pockets and the boom mic.

gallery.caption: The pod on the left of a modular helmet (a white stand-in), behind the chin bar's pivot: stuck on with VHB tape, no holes
The pod: 102 × 37 mm and 16.5 mm proud of the shell at its middle, 3 rubber domes in a screwed lid, the USB-C plug at its back end, the cables out of its bottom
Opened up: the lid, the TPU keypad (also the gasket), the switch board, the neckband's board and the battery
Inside (the stand-in cut open): a speaker puck in the left ear pocket, the boom mic held low on the fixed shell, reaching into the chin bar
The parts that go inside: a speaker puck with a 40 mm speaker, the boom mount and the mic cup

docs.label: README: what goes where, the neckband, the pod, wiring, build order

pod_body.name: Pod body
pod_body.what: Holds the neckband's board, its battery and the switch board. Its underside is curved to the shell and stuck on with VHB tape; the USB-C hole at its back end, 2 cable holes in its bottom wall; 4 pillars for M2 heat-set inserts
pod_body.material: PETG or ASA, a light colour if you can. Open side down

pod_lid.name: Pod lid
pod_lid.what: Rolled edges, 3 holes for the keypad's domes, ridges between them; 4 M2 × 6 countersunk screws

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: One TPU sheet: its 3 hollow domes are the buttons (the big middle one is play/pause and calls) and its edge is the seam's gasket, squeezed 0.2 mm by the lid

usb_plug.name: USB-C plug
usb_plug.what: Seals the USB-C socket when you ride; pull it out by its tab to charge

speaker_puck.name: Speaker puck
speaker_puck.what: Holds a 40 mm speaker (closed back) in the liner's ear pocket, on a Velcro dot

mic_cup.name: Mic cup
mic_cup.what: Holds the mic capsule on the end of the boom; a foam windscreen goes over it

boom_mount.name: Boom mount
boom_mount.what: A thin plate that slides between the shell and the liner (or sticks to the shell) low on the left, behind the chin bar; the boom pushes into its socket

headset_assembled.name: Pod, assembled
headset_assembled.what: The pod with its keypad, lid and plug

params.name: shell_rl
params.label: Shell's radius along the pod (front to back)
params.help: Lay a ruler across the spot: radius = L × L / (8 × gap) + gap / 2.

params.name: shell_rw
params.label: Shell's radius across the pod (up and down)

params.name: nb_over
params.label: Tallest part on the board (not the USB-C)

params.name: usb_out
params.label: USB-C socket past the board's end

params.name: batt_l
params.label: Battery length
params.help: The neckband's own battery, or a 502540 LiPo (40 × 25 × 5).

params.help: 40 mm helmet speakers; the earbuds' own drivers are about 13 × 4 (quiet).
